Write $\rho_p=\operatorname{diag}(1-p,p)$ for a diagonal qubit state. Set $a=\pi/12$ and
$$\mathcal S_a=\{\rho_{\sin^2\theta}:a\le\theta\le\pi/4\},\qquad T_a(\rho_{\sin^2\theta})=\rho_{\sin^2(\theta-a)}.$$
On this family, $T_a$ preserves root fidelity and contracts trace distance for every pair, but it sends the finite input relative entropy $D(\rho_{\sin^2(\pi/4)}\|\rho_{\sin^2 a})$ to $D(\rho_{\sin^2(\pi/4-a)}\|\rho_0)=+\infty$. The map is nonlinear and is not the restriction of a quantum channel. Thus metric inequalities on a family under an arbitrary map do not by themselves prove quantum-relative-entropy data processing for channels.

As a separate support check, $|0\rangle\langle0|$ and $|+\rangle\langle+|$ have root fidelity and trace distance both $1/\sqrt2$, while $D(|0\rangle\langle0|\| |+\rangle\langle+|)=+\infty$.

For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) whose unique adjoint $P^*$ exists by [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]], and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

Let $\omega_{ZA}$ be any finite-dimensional state with $\operatorname{Tr}_Z\omega_{ZA}=\rho_A$, and let $|\psi\rangle_{RA}$ purify $\rho_A$ with $R$ a copy of $A$. There is a CPTP map $\Lambda:R\to Z$ with $(\Lambda\otimes\operatorname{id}_A)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)=\omega_{ZA}$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $(E_y)_{y\in\Omega}$ be a finite POVM on $H$, where $\Omega=\{y_0,\ldots,y_{m-1}\}$ is a fixed enumeration of its nonempty outcome set. Let $K=\mathbb C^m$ with standard orthonormal basis $(f_0,\ldots,f_{m-1})$, and set $\Pi_jz:=\langle z,f_j\rangle f_j$, the rank-one projection onto $f_j$ under the root linear-first convention. The map $\mathcal M_E(X):=\sum_{j<m}\operatorname{tr}(XE_{y_j})\Pi_j$ is a quantum channel from $H$ to $K$. For the indexed register $\mathbb C^\Omega$ with orthonormal basis $|y\rangle$, the unitary identification $Jf_j=|y_j\rangle$ gives the equivalent channel $X\mapsto\sum_{y\in\Omega}\operatorname{tr}(E_yX)|y\rangle\langle y|=J\mathcal M_E(X)J^*$. Thus either finite outcome-register convention is covered.

Let $D\ge2$, $1\le K\le D$, and $\omega_{AE}\succeq0$ with $\dim A=D$, $\operatorname{tr}\omega\le1$, and $r=\operatorname{rank}\omega_E$. For every $\delta>0$ there is an explicitly specified finite probability ensemble of isometries $W:\mathbb C^K\to\mathbb C^D$ such that, for
$$\omega^W_{RE}=\frac DK(W^T\otimes I_E)\omega_{AE}(\overline W\otimes I_E),$$
one has
$$\mathbb E\left\|\omega^W_{RE}-\frac{I_R}{K}\otimes\omega_E\right\|_1\le\sqrt{2Kr\operatorname{tr}(\omega_{AE}^2)}+\delta.$$
At the same time the ensemble can be required to satisfy, for every Hermitian $Z_{AE}$,
$$\mathbb E\left\|\frac DK(W^T\otimes I)Z(\overline W\otimes I)\right\|_1\le(1+\delta)\|Z\|_1.$$
No Haar existence or Gaussian-law supplier, and no choice axiom, is used.

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $T:K\to K$ be positive definite, and let $V:H\to K$ satisfy $V^*V=I_H$. For every $s\ge0$,

$$V^*(T+sI_K)^{-1}V\succeq(V^*TV+sI_H)^{-1},$$

where $A\succeq B$ means that $A-B$ is non-negative. If $H=\{0\}$, both sides are the unique endomorphism of $H$.

Let $V:H\to K$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces satisfying $V^*V=I_H$, and let $A,B$ be non-negative on $H$. Then

$$D(VAV^*\|VBV^*)=D(A\|B).$$

Let $A,B$ be positive-definite operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$. On $\mathcal L(H)$, with Hilbert-Schmidt inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle_{\rm HS}:=\operatorname{tr}(XY^*)$, define $\Delta_{B,A}(X):=BXA^{-1}$. Then $\Delta_{B,A}$ is positive definite and

$$D(A\|B)=\langle(-\ln\Delta_{B,A})(A^{1/2}),A^{1/2}\rangle_{\rm HS}.$$

The logarithm of $\Delta_{B,A}$ is defined by its positive eigenvalues.

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $T:K\to K$ be positive definite, and let $V:H\to K$ satisfy $V^*V=I_H$. Then, in the non-negative operator order,

$$-\ln(V^*TV)\preceq V^*(-\ln T)V,$$

where $R\preceq S$ means $S-R$ is non-negative and logarithms of positive-definite operators are defined by finite spectral calculus.

For a finite-dimensional bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$,

$$I(A:B)_\rho=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB})=D(\rho_{AB}\|\rho_A\otimes\rho_B).$$

For a finite classical-quantum state $\rho_{XB}=\sum_xp_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x$, its mutual information equals its Holevo information:

$$I(X:B)_\rho=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x)=\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}).$$

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $n\ge1$, let $A_i,B_i:H\to H$ be non-negative for $1\le i\le n$, and let $\lambda_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. Then, in the extended-real order,

$$D\!\left(\sum_i\lambda_iA_i\,\middle\|\,\sum_i\lambda_iB_i\right)\le\sum_i\lambda_iD(A_i\|B_i),$$

where zero-weight terms are omitted from the right side, and the order is that on the extended real line.

Let $H_A,H_B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $d=\dim H_B\ge1$, and let $A,B$ be non-negative operators on $H_A\otimes H_B$. Then

$$D(\operatorname{Tr}_B A\|\operatorname{Tr}_B B)\le D(A\|B).$$

Let $H_A,H_B,H_C$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a density operator on their ordered tensor product. Write $\rho_{AB},\rho_{BC},\rho_B$ for its marginals using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]]. Then
$$S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})\ge S(\rho_B)+S(\rho_{ABC}),$$
where $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho)$ with $0\ln0:=0$ as in [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

Let $H,K$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be a quantum channel ([[def-qc-quantum-channel]]), and let $A,B$ be non-negative operators on $H$. Then

$$D(\Phi(A)\|\Phi(B))\le D(A\|B).$$

On the qubit space with computational basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, define the dephasing channel
$$\Delta(X)=|0\rangle\langle0|X|0\rangle\langle0|+|1\rangle\langle1|X|1\rangle\langle1|.$$
For $|+\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and $\rho=|+\rangle\langle+|$, $\sigma=\operatorname{diag}(3/4,1/4)$, one has
$$D(\rho\|\sigma)=\tfrac12\ln(16/3)>\tfrac12\ln(4/3)=D(\Delta(\rho)\|\Delta(\sigma)).$$
For the orthogonal pure states $|+\rangle,| -\rangle=(|0\rangle-|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$, the input relative entropy is $+\infty$, whereas both dephased states equal $I/2$ and their relative entropy is $0$.

Let $\mathcal N_i:A_i\to B_i$ for $i=1,2$ be finite-dimensional degradable channels with complements $\mathcal N_i^c=\mathcal D_i\circ\mathcal N_i$. Then $\rho\mapsto I_c(\rho,\mathcal N_i)$ is concave and nonnegative. For every joint input state $\rho_{A_1A_2}$,

$$I_c(\rho_{A_1A_2},\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)\le I_c(\rho_{A_1},\mathcal N_1)+I_c(\rho_{A_2},\mathcal N_2).$$

Consequently the supremum coherent information of $\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2$ is the sum of the two single-channel suprema.

Fix any finite input ensemble $(p_x,\rho_x)$ for a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N$ and a complement $\mathcal N^c$. Let $\chi_B,\chi_E$ be the Holevo informations of their output ensembles. Every $0<R<\chi_B-\chi_E$ admits uniform $M_n$-message codes with mixed input states, Bob POVMs, $n^{-1}\ln M_n\to R$, average error tending to zero, and unnormalized complementary-output Holevo leakage tending to zero. The construction has exponentially decaying average error and average trace distance to a fixed complementary product target; dimension-dependent entropy control converts the latter to strong Holevo secrecy.

Let $\tau=JJ^*/D$ be the flat state of a nonzero $D$-dimensional input subspace of a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N$. With prior shared maximally entangled states on that subspace, every $0\le R<S(\tau)+I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)$ is achievable for classical messages with average error tending to zero. The code consists of finite Weyl operations followed by a collective output/reference POVM; it has rate tending to $R$.
